focus_topics: tactile visible physics demonstrations (magnets in copper, acoustic levitation, Leidenfrost, ferrofluid-like physical shockers)
impossible material strength, fluid dynamics, wave & optical illusions
high-stakes cosmic limits (speed of light, extreme gravity, sound waves)
avoid_angles: abstract invisible quantum jargon without dramatic physical visuals
neuroscience or psychology topics unrelated to physical demonstrations
lecture titles starting with 'The Physics of...'
repeating quantum levitation, superconductors, Prince Rupert's Drop, or Mpemba effect
physics.hook_style: Use tactile contrast titles like 'The [Concrete Object] That [Impossible Action]!' or 'How [Force] [Shocking Verb] [Object]!'
physics.extra_directive: Prioritize visible physical effects viewers can immediately see bend, levitate, shatter, spike, or glow in the first 2 seconds.

focus_topics: extreme visible thermal or phase-change contrasts (burning-hot ice, rainbow crystal metals, liquid metals)
dramatic fiery, luminous, hydrophobic, or self-healing material transformations
shocking hidden chemistry inside everyday solids and liquids
avoid_angles: invisible gases or invisible timers that look empty on camera
mild 'changes color' phrasing without extreme stakes
chemistry.hook_style: Use extreme visual contrast titles: 'The [Liquid/Metal/Material] That [Impossible Visual Action]!'
chemistry.extra_directive: NEVER choose invisible phenomena. Every topic must produce a striking, colorful, fiery, crystalline, or physically bizarre visual transformation.

focus_topics: deep-ocean predators, camouflage masters, and marine bioluminescence
extreme insect weapons and survival superpowers (boiling sprays, supersonic snaps, regeneration)
avoid_angles: human body organs, digestion, brain, throat, or medical anatomy (4x-6x lower views and moderation risk)
confusing metaphors or hyperbolic clickbait titles ('flies to the moon')
repeating immortal jellyfish / animals that never grow old
biology.hook_style: Spotlight one concrete organism's real superpower: 'The Ocean's [Archetype]' or 'The [Creature/Plant] That [Shocking Real Action]!'
biology.extra_directive: Focus 100% on wild animals, marine life, insects, microbes, and extreme plants with concrete shocking comparisons (e.g., louder than a jet, fires boiling liquid).

focus_topics: rule-breaking physical wonders (defying gravity, breaking light speed in water, sonoluminescence)
jaw-dropping prehistoric and planetary science shocks (natural nuclear reactors, ancient atmospheric events)
counterintuitive survival or danger physics myth-busts (liquid nitrogen Leidenfrost, extreme materials)
avoid_angles: dry textbook titles ending in 'Explained' or starting with 'Why Water...'
mundane everyday gadget trivia or vague 'also a gas' phrasing
repeating supercooled water, gallium melting in hand, or Mpemba effect
general_science.hook_style: Use rule-breaking curiosity titles: 'The [Thing] That [Breaks Famous Law]!', 'Earth's [Shocking Hidden Fact]', or 'Can [Ordinary Thing] Create [Extreme Thing]?'
general_science.extra_directive: Frame every topic as a jaw-dropping real anomaly or broken rule of nature—never like a school textbook explanation.

focus_topics: hidden deep-Earth structures (LLSVPs, underground oceans, ancient mantle anomalies)
extreme volcanic, tectonic, glacial, and deep-trench phenomena (underwater waterfalls, blue-lava volcanoes, mega-caverns)
epic prehistoric Earth events and bizarre geological time capsules
avoid_angles: dull textbook geography definitions or generic weather reports
flat lowercase declarative titles without a curiosity hook
earth_science.hook_style: Use epic Title Case curiosity titles: 'Earth's Hidden [Extreme Feature]!', 'The Place on Earth Where [Impossible Geological Event]!', or 'Earth Built Its Own [Shocking Thing]'
earth_science.extra_directive: Lead Beat 1 with dramatic real geological cinematography (lava, deep canyons, glaciers, lightning supercells, crystals) and make Earth feel alien and awe-inspiring.

focus_topics: extreme and lethal cosmic objects (magnetars, hypervelocity stars, vampire stars, tidal disruption events)
bizarre exoplanets (molten iron/glass rain, eyeball worlds, pitch-black planets, rogue worlds)
mind-bending deep-space mysteries (Boötes Void, neutron star mountains, gravitational lensing, JWST anomalies)
avoid_angles: overdone basic trivia like Neptune diamond rain or 'more stars than grains of sand'
astronomy.hook_style: Use high-stakes cosmic titles: 'The Alien World That [Extreme Phenomenon]', 'The Dead Star That [Lethal Action]', or 'The Most Terrifying [Object] in Space'
astronomy.extra_directive: Maximize cosmic scale and danger/wonder in the first 2 seconds; pair vivid deep-space NASA/observatory visuals with surprising astrophysical numbers.
